event.details: The king asks who first practiced and disclosed the vow and what merit/results it gives. Brahmā says Pārvatī practiced at Śiva’s instruction for four months when Skanda was gone and saw Kārttikeya in the fifth. Agastya desiring to drink the ocean practiced and drank it through Vighneśa’s favour in three months. Damayantī searching for Nala practiced for six months and then saw him. These are brief source reports; no unprovided journeys or battle details are added.
event.outcome: Three retrospective exempla give specific practice intervals and actual reported outcomes.

event.details: Citralekhā had taken Pradyumna’s son away. Grieving and uncertain where or by whom he was taken, Pradyumna hears Rukmiṇī address him as her son. She recalls Śambara abducting him when he was six days old, many years of grief and comparisons with other women’s growing sons, then Lomaśa’s fortunate visit and instruction in Sankaṣṭa-caturthī. She practiced four times; through its favour Pradyumna returned after killing Śambara in battle. She urges him to practice the same vow so he will learn where his son is.
event.outcome: Rukmiṇī’s retrospective rescue experience becomes explicit mother-to-son instruction for a new search.

event.details: Brahmā says Pradyumna practices the pleasing vow and hears from Nārada that the son is detained in Bāṇāsura’s city. At Uddhava’s instruction Kṛṣṇa, fearing a battle with Īśvara, properly practices the vow once. He goes to Śoṇitapura, defeats Bāṇāsura in combat, and quickly brings Aniruddha with Uṣā.
event.outcome: Nārada locates the detained son; one vow, actual combat victory and retrieval follow. No weapons or marriage ceremony are supplied here.

event.details: Brahmā says he too performed the vow desiring creation and produced varied creation through its power. Gods, asuras, humans, sages, Dānavas, Yakṣas, Kinnaras, Uragas and Rākṣasas also practiced to quell obstacles. He instructs practice during distress, hearing the story, silent eating with hands between knees while meditating Gaṇeśa, and sharing the Brahmins’ remainder with relatives. Tasks accomplish in few months. Teach neither non-devotees, atheists nor deceitful people, but a son, pupil or virtuous devotee. Calling the king dear, righteous and a worker for public good, Brahmā says to perform this before other vows; men and women should perform it before intended tasks.
event.outcome: Reported creation and wider practitioners support instructions, timing and transmission restrictions.
